findings.source_passage: Nobody spoke for a minute; then Meg said in an altered tone,--
findings.source_locator: paragraph 6, before Meg's speech about sacrifices
findings.why_it_matters: The beat of silence and the narratorial note of Meg's 'altered tone' establish the tonal shift from grumbling to sober reflection; its removal flattens the scene's emotional pacing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence 'Nobody spoke for a minute; then Meg said in an altered tone,—' before Meg's speech about sacrifices.

findings.source_passage: which no one heard but the hearth-brush and kettle-holder
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Jo's bookworm line, Beth's sigh
findings.why_it_matters: This whimsical, personifying aside is a signature stylistic touch—Alcott's playful comic narrator voice; its deletion flattens the prose to plain report.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical 'which no one heard but the hearth-brush and kettle-holder' to Beth's line about new music.

findings.source_passage: a good picture or two hung on the walls, books filled the recesses
findings.why_it_matters: The draft omits the detail about pictures on the walls from the room description, slightly thinning the establishing sketch of the comfortable modest home that carries interpretive weight about the March family's genteel poverty.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'a good picture or two hung on the walls' back into the room description.

findings.source_passage: Her father called her 'Little Tranquillity,' and the name suited her excellently
findings.why_it_matters: The draft uses 'Little Tranquillity' as a bare label without the full sentence explaining the father gave her this name and why it suited her—losing the warmth and interpretive framing of Beth's character.

findings.source_passage: What the characters of the four sisters were we will leave to be found out.
findings.why_it_matters: This closing narratorial wink is a well-known voice-establishing moment—the narrator directly addressing the reader with playful irony; its loss erases a signature register marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the closing line 'What the characters of the four sisters were we will leave to be found out.' at the end of the character sketch paragraph.

findings.source_passage: Jo tossed up her napkin, crying, 'A letter! a letter! Three cheers for father!'
findings.source_locator: supper scene, Mrs. March announces the treat
findings.why_it_matters: The draft reverses the order—gives the letter content first, then Jo's cry—and omits 'tossed up her napkin', losing the vivid physicality and the exact exclamatory rhythm of a culturally recognizable moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sequence: first Jo's cry with napkin-tossing, then Mrs. March's description of the letter contents.

findings.source_passage: Jo, rolling her eyes and clutching at the air, as she had seen a famous tragedian do
findings.why_it_matters: The Macbeth riff ('Is that a dagger that I see before me?') and the stage business are cut entirely; though the rehearsal scene is compressed, this comic highlight is signature Alcott wit.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Jo's Macbeth moment ('Is that a dagger that I see before me?') with the stage-business detail into the rehearsal paragraph.

findings.source_passage: for the mother was a born singer. The first sound in the morning was her voice, as she went about the house singing like a lark
findings.why_it_matters: The draft collapses the passage into a vague summary, losing 'singing like a lark' and the full warmth of the closing image of Marmee's voice as the household's sonic frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'for the mother was a born singer. The first sound in the morning was her voice, as she went about the house singing like a lark' in the final paragraph.

summary: The draft preserves the chapter's major plot beats and most signature lines but accumulates five medium-severity voice-flattening losses—the silence beat before Meg's altered-tone speech, the comic hearth-brush parenthetical, the 'what the characters were we leave to be found out' narratorial wink, the reversal of the letter-announcement sequence, and the compression of Beth's character-sketch framing—which together erode the narrator's distinctive playful register and trigger regeneration.
